creator_or_organization: Publicis Groupe and Groupe Les Echos
language: Multilingual (French and English, with 170+ nationalities represented)
content_focus: VivaTech covers the full spectrum of technology and innovation with a strong AI emphasis. Key themes include artificial intelligence (keynotes, workshops, LLM deep-dives, AI startup showcases), quantum computing, robotics, deep tech infrastructure, sustainability, digital transformation, and ethical tech. The event features startup challenges, product launches and world-premiere demos, corporate innovation showcases (LVMH, L'Oreal, Orange), and investor-startup matchmaking. In 2025, there was a 40% surge in AI exhibitors, and NVIDIA co-hosted GTC Paris within VivaTech, where Mistral Compute (European AI infrastructure by NVIDIA and Mistral AI) was announced. Content is organized across multiple pavilions and stages including an Exec Arena, CMO Lounge, and Tech Leaders Lounge.
target_audience: Entrepreneurs, startup founders, corporate executives (CEOs, CTOs, CMOs), investors and VCs, business leaders, students and academics, and the general public (on the final day). Designed to bridge technical innovation with business strategy.
publication_frequency: Event-based (annual, held in June in Paris)
format_and_length: 4-day in-person conference at Paris Expo Porte de Versailles. First 3 days are for professionals (startups, investors, executives, students, academics); the 4th day (Saturday) is open to the general public. Format includes keynotes, panel discussions, full-day workshops, exhibition halls, startup challenges and pitch competitions, networking lounges, and product demos. 450+ speakers per edition. Typical hours: 9am-6pm.
accessibility_for_non_engineers: High. VivaTech is explicitly designed to bridge business and technology. Content ranges from high-level keynotes by CEOs and world leaders (Emmanuel Macron, Jensen Huang) to hands-on demos accessible to non-technical visitors. The Exec Arena features business case studies, and the CMO and Tech Leaders Lounges cater to non-engineering executives. Business-framed discussions on AI strategy, digital transformation, and innovation make it highly approachable for business students and entrepreneurs without deep technical backgrounds.
signal_to_noise_ratio: Medium. The sheer scale (180,000 attendees, 14,000 startups, 4,000 exhibitors) means there is a lot of content and it can feel overwhelming. The keynotes and curated tracks are high-signal, but the exhibition floor mixes cutting-edge innovation with marketing noise. Careful session selection is key to extracting maximum value.
unique_value_proposition: Europe's largest tech and startup conference, uniquely positioned at the intersection of French/European tech ecosystem and global innovation. It is the premier venue for: (1) seeing the entire European AI startup landscape in one place, (2) hearing from both American tech giants (NVIDIA, Meta, OpenAI) and European champions (Mistral AI, BlaBlaCar, OVHcloud), (3) direct access to 3,600+ investors including Accel, KKR, Lightspeed, Sequoia Capital, and Google Ventures, and (4) policy discussions with French and EU officials on AI regulation and digital sovereignty. No other European conference combines this scale of startup showcasing, corporate innovation, and policy dialogue.
free_or_paid: Paid. Standard passes range from approximately 200-650 EUR (excl. VAT) depending on timing and pass type. VIP passes up to ~1,000 EUR with lounge access and premium networking. Startup exhibition corners cost ~3,500 EUR. Some free passes available for students via partner institutions (e.g., HEC Paris) and startup challenge winners. The Saturday public day requires a separate (lower-cost) ticket.
source_reliability: High. VivaTech is co-organized by Publicis Groupe (a global communications leader) and Groupe Les Echos (France's leading business media group, publisher of Les Echos newspaper). The event is backed by the French government, with regular participation from the President of France and ministers. Speakers are vetted C-level executives, researchers, and policymakers from world-leading organizations. The event's announcements (e.g., Mistral Compute) are covered by major international media.
relevance_for_entrepreneurs: Extremely high for AI entrepreneurs. VivaTech is the premier European event for: (1) discovering the latest AI products, tools, and infrastructure before competitors, (2) networking with 3,600+ investors and capital funds for fundraising, (3) benchmarking your startup against 14,000 others across 30+ industries, (4) understanding corporate AI adoption priorities from major enterprises (LVMH, L'Oreal, ManpowerGroup), (5) getting visibility through startup challenges and pitch competitions, (6) understanding European AI regulation and policy direction directly from officials, and (7) making strategic connections — the 2025 edition facilitated 640,000 business connections.
actionable_insight_level: High. The event produces concrete takeaways: product launches to evaluate, partnerships to pursue, investor contacts to follow up with, regulatory insights to plan around, and technology trends to incorporate into business strategy. Over 300 announcements were made at VivaTech 2025 alone.
session_mapping: Cross-session (S1: AI landscape and ecosystem actors; S3: AI project framing with real startup examples; S4: AI business models and startup scaling; S5: EU AI Act and governance discussions with policymakers)
ecosystem_position: Primary source and ecosystem hub. VivaTech is not an aggregator or educational platform — it is a live marketplace where the AI ecosystem converges. It functions as a primary source for product announcements and launches, a networking infrastructure connecting startups with corporates and investors, and a policy forum for European tech governance. It is the definitive annual checkpoint for the state of European AI and tech innovation.
recommendation_tier: Nice-to-Have (attend in person if possible, especially the AI tracks and startup challenges; otherwise follow the announcements and keynote recordings online after the event. For M2 Entrepreneurship students in Paris, attending the Saturday public day is strongly recommended as a hands-on learning experience.)
